facts.text: In 1902 Willis Carrier, a young engineer at the Buffalo Forge Company, was asked to fix a humidity problem at a printing company in Brooklyn, New York.
At the printing plant, humid summer air made the paper swell and the printed colors blur.
Carrier's system blew air over cold coils so that extra moisture condensed out; making people comfortable was a side effect that raised wider interest.
Early systems were used in industry, for example to control humidity and temperature in textile mills; at first they were too large and expensive for homes.
In the 1920s many American movie theaters installed cooling, and theaters were where most members of the public first felt cooled air.
Air conditioning moved into private homes mainly after World War II.
In the late 1960s, more affordable air conditioning helped fuel population growth in hot states such as Arizona and Florida.
Before air conditioning, people spent hot evenings outdoors, including on front porches, and some slept on roofs or lawns; afterwards families retreated into houses with shut windows.
Air conditioning made sealed buildings with fixed glass windows practical.
Air conditioning is described as the strongest protective factor against heat-related illness.
A 2014 ASU study of Phoenix found that waste heat released by air conditioners raised nighttime air temperatures, which in turn raised demand for cooling, a feedback loop.
Shade trees and cool roofs made of light-colored or reflective materials lower surface and air temperatures and reduce the need for air conditioning.

notes: 混合題 mixed-top-02 第 1 組用（2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句）。Carrier 的機器最初是為了控制濕度而不是讓人涼快，選文照這個寫；Phoenix 研究的升溫幅度選文不寫數字，只寫夜間氣溫升高與惡性循環。EPA 頁面 2026-10-09 以搜尋結果確認內容（樹木遮蔭、淺色反光屋頂降溫）。
